22870-opacity-and-score-gradient-computa.summary: Opacity and Score Gradient Computation calculates gradients for opacity parameters in differentiable volume rendering, distinguishing itself by handling non-linear opacity interactions in Time-of-Flight models and explicit mask modulation.

4254-maskgaussian-gradient-computation.m.summary: MaskGaussian Gradient Computation computes loss gradients for learnable Gaussian masks, differing from standard backpropagation by explicitly accounting for mask contributions to both foreground color and background transmittance.

11915-3d-gaussian-splatting-as-markov-ch.name: 3D Gaussian Splatting as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
11915-3d-gaussian-splatting-as-markov-ch.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting as Markov Chain Monte Carlo reinterprets training as sampling, enabling discrete structural changes via MCMC moves to avoid gradient-based discontinuities.

12071-cross-structure-collaboration-modu.summary: The Cross-Structure Collaboration Module integrates global tri-plane features with local context grids to generate hierarchical dense embedded features, solving misalignment in large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting.

9445-contribution-based-pruning.md.summary: Contribution-based Pruning removes redundant 3D Gaussian primitives by jointly evaluating opacity and scale, unlike methods relying on single criteria.

23289-scale-and-resolution-aware-redunda.summary: This method prunes redundant 3D Gaussian primitives by modeling the relationship between camera resolution, primitive scale, and local density to determine necessity.

1022-homogeneous-medium-transmittance.md.summary: Homogeneous Medium Transmittance computes radiance survival through a uniform medium using simple multiplication, unlike heterogeneous models that require integration.

5639-transfer-function-ensembles.md.summary: Transfer Function Ensembles merge multiple scalar-value transfer functions using weighted ADD, AND, or XOR operations to create a single complex mapping.

5637-multi-space-transfer-function-blend.name: Multi-Space Transfer Function Blending (Hardware Limitation Approach)
5637-multi-space-transfer-function-blend.summary: Multi-Space Transfer Function Blending combines transfer functions from up to three unique data spaces into a single 3D RGBA texture, constrained by hardware texture limits.

7265-style-aggregation.md.name: Style Aggregation
7265-style-aggregation.md.summary: Style Aggregation sums fuzzy membership functions to unify semantic contributions into a crisp rendering parameter, distinguished by its reliance on fuzzy logic implication rather than hardware-limited blending.

11685-t-conorms-aggregation-functions.md.name: T-conorms (Aggregation Functions)
11685-t-conorms-aggregation-functions.md.summary: T-conorms are continuous, differentiable aggregation functions that generalize the logical 'or' to combine face occupancy probabilities, providing smooth gradients for gradient-based optimization in volume rendering.

5932-probabilistic-and-statistical-model.name: Probabilistic and Statistical Modeling
5932-probabilistic-and-statistical-model.summary: Probabilistic and Statistical Modeling replaces hard threshold-based classification with statistical distributions or machine learning models to map volume data features to optical properties, addressing ambiguity in material signatures.

5458-clustering-based-gray-gradient-tran.name: Clustering-Based Gray-Gradient Transfer Function
5458-clustering-based-gray-gradient-tran.summary: Clustering-Based Gray-Gradient Transfer Function automatically generates a 2D transfer function by clustering a gray-gradient histogram to map tissue zones, eliminating manual design and preserving edge details.

6287-support-vector-machine-svm-classifi.name: Support Vector Machine (SVM) Classification
6287-support-vector-machine-svm-classifi.summary: SVM classification maps volume data to optical properties by finding an optimal separating hyperplane, offering global minimum solutions and superior data efficiency compared to neural networks.

8593-information-based-transfer-function.name: Information-based Transfer Function Fusion
8593-information-based-transfer-function.summary: Information-based Transfer Function Fusion automates multimodal volume visualization by fusing multiple registered modalities into a single scalar value using information theory, distinguishing itself by defining an information channel between input datasets rather than discarding one.

9731-information-theory-based-multimodal.name: Information Theory-Based Multimodal Transfer Function Design
9731-information-theory-based-multimodal.summary: This automated method designs multimodal transfer functions by using mutual information decomposition to fuse complementary data, ensuring both inputs are represented in a single coherent visualization.

9279-probabilistic-classification-model-.name: Probabilistic Classification Model for Volume Data
9279-probabilistic-classification-model-.summary: This model resolves single-voxel ambiguity by assigning conditional probabilities to feature classes and integrating them into kernel regression for feature-specific scalar reconstruction before optical mapping.

9488-statistical-metrics-based-transfer-.name: Statistical Metrics-based Transfer Function
9488-statistical-metrics-based-transfer-.summary: Statistical Metrics-based Transfer Function maps volume data to optical properties using local neighborhood statistics like mean and variance, enabling intuitive feature separation beyond scalar intensity.

12205-statistical-signatures.md.name: Statistical Signatures
12205-statistical-signatures.md.summary: Statistical Signatures automatically specifies transfer functions by characterizing voxels via local neighborhood metrics like mean and standard deviation, rather than scalar values alone.

11686-distribution-families-for-differen.name: Distribution Families for Differentiable Rendering
11686-distribution-families-for-differen.summary: This family provides a unified library of smooth, differentiable distribution families for transfer functions in volume rendering, enabling gradient flow through opacity assignment.

15187-split-conformal-prediction-calibra.name: Split Conformal Prediction Calibration
15187-split-conformal-prediction-calibra.summary: Split Conformal Prediction Calibration is a post-hoc method that adjusts uncertainty estimates in neural radiance fields using a held-out set to ensure provable, distribution-free coverage guarantees.

15189-gaussian-mixture-models.md.name: Gaussian Mixture Models
15189-gaussian-mixture-models.md.summary: Gaussian Mixture Models are parametric statistical models for uncertainty visualization in volume rendering that balance memory constraints against classification quality, serving as a compact baseline compared to nonparametric alternatives.

1812-gaussian-sum-transfer-function.md.name: Gaussian Sum Transfer Function
1812-gaussian-sum-transfer-function.md.summary: The Gaussian Sum Transfer Function maps scalar values to RGBA by summing Gaussian functions, allowing explicit control points to define smooth, multi-modal classification boundaries in volume rendering.

4330-gaussian-transfer-function-componen.summary: A Gaussian Transfer Function Component is a single Gaussian function defining opacity in a 1D transfer function, distinguished by its parameterization via mean, sigma, and height factor.

6243-gaussian-transfer-function-composit.summary: Gaussian Transfer Function Composition is an interactive method for constructing multi-dimensional transfer functions by blending 2D Gaussian opacity functions on a pre-computed dimensional reduction map.

4663-generalized-exponential-transfer-fu.name: Generalized Exponential Transfer Function
4663-generalized-exponential-transfer-fu.summary: The Generalized Exponential Transfer Function is a parametric volume rendering component that generalizes Gaussian mixtures by introducing a learnable shape parameter to adapt tail behavior for sharp edges and band-unlimited signals.

4681-laplacian-of-gaussian-mixture-model.name: Laplacian of Gaussian Mixture Model
4681-laplacian-of-gaussian-mixture-model.summary: The Laplacian of Gaussian Mixture Model is a probabilistic transfer function that uses Mexican hat-shaped basis functions to enhance edge detection and feature highlighting in volume rendering.

21595-peak-based-transfer-function-model.name: Peak-based Transfer Function Model
21595-peak-based-transfer-function-model.summary: The Peak-based Transfer Function Model defines a transfer function as a sum of sinusoidal window functions, offering intuitive control for hand-held devices unlike Gaussian-based alternatives.

5862-local-data-models-for-probabilistic.name: Local Data Models for Probabilistic Transfer Function Design
5862-local-data-models-for-probabilistic.summary: Local Data Models for Probabilistic Transfer Function Design is an interactive technique that fits variable Gaussian Mixture Models to user-specified local data subsets, avoiding the overgeneralization of global methods.

20039-neighborhood-weighted-gaussian-mix.name: Neighborhood Weighted Gaussian Mixture Model
20039-neighborhood-weighted-gaussian-mix.summary: The Neighborhood Weighted Gaussian Mixture Model classifies vectorial volumes by weighting class probabilities with neighboring voxel data to enforce spatial continuity and reduce noise sensitivity.

20292-splat-regression.md.name: Splat Regression
20292-splat-regression.md.summary: Splat Regression models functions using anisotropic bump functions optimized via Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao gradients, distinguishing itself by allowing local shape adjustments unlike standard Gaussian Mixture Models.

22711-gabor-fields.md.name: Gabor Fields
22711-gabor-fields.md.summary: Gabor Fields represent volumetric density using Gaussian and Gabor kernels to enable continuous level-of-detail via primitive pruning and orientation-selective filtering, avoiding the re-fitting required by Gaussian-based methods.

22726-gabor-kernel-fourier-transform.md.summary: The Gabor Kernel Fourier Transform computes the analytical frequency-domain representation of a Gabor kernel, distinguishing itself by decoupling Gaussian spread from oscillatory frequency for precise orientation and scale control.

6103-pre-classification.md.name: Pre-classification
6103-pre-classification.md.summary: Pre-classification maps voxel values to optical properties before ray casting, preventing color bleeding but suppressing high-frequency details.

6120-fuzzy-logic-rule-based-semantic-lay.name: Fuzzy-Logic Rule Based Semantic Layer

6430-fuzzy-set-based-volume-selection-an.summary: This method uses fuzzy set arithmetic to define Selection, Ghost, and Background volumes, isolating intersection regions to apply custom blending rules that keep transformed objects visually distinct from their original positions and the background.

7040-artistic-volume-rendering-template..name: Artistic Volume Rendering Template
7040-artistic-volume-rendering-template..summary: Artistic Volume Rendering Template maps volumetric data to visual styles using fuzzy-logic rules and composites prioritized shader templates, differing from standard methods by decoupling color evaluation into layered artistic styles.

7439-semantics-by-analogy.md.name: Semantics by Analogy

12072-nrff.md.name: NRFF

12095-semantic-and-feature-branches.md.summary: Semantic and Feature Branches extend NeRF by predicting arbitrary per-point feature signals alongside density and color, providing a general mechanism for embedding high-dimensional feature spaces into volumetric representations.

13619-said-nerf.md.name: SAID-NeRF
13619-said-nerf.md.summary: SAID-NeRF is a semantic radiance field method that uses Visual Foundation Model masks to enhance surface estimation for transparent objects by jointly optimizing a semantic field for sharper depth and diffuse color.

13661-mine.md.name: MINE
13661-mine.md.summary: MINE is a hybrid method combining Multi-Plane Images with Neural Radiance Fields to reconstruct 3D representations from single images, offering efficiency independent of target view count.

13738-voxel-and-sparse-grid-representati.summary: Voxel and Sparse Grid Representations replace implicit neural networks with explicit spatial structures to enable real-time rendering and scale to large scenes.

13480-g-nelf.md.name: G-NeLF
13480-g-nelf.md.summary: G-NeLF is a memory-efficient novel view synthesis method that predicts ray color directly using a hash-based tri-plane and LSTM, bypassing volume density modeling.

14267-scalar-nerf.md.name: SCALAR-NeRF

14761-tridf.md.name: TriDF

15219-tile-and-slide-framework.md.name: Tile and Slide Framework

13911-transformer-and-vision-model-integ.name: Transformer and Vision Model Integration
13911-transformer-and-vision-model-integ.summary: Transformer and Vision Model Integration replaces standard NeRF MLPs with vision backbones to enable generalizable novel view synthesis from single images without per-scene optimization.

13878-vit-nerf.md.name: ViT-NeRF
13878-vit-nerf.md.summary: ViT-NeRF is a view synthesis method combining a Vision Transformer for global shape and a CNN for local appearance, producing sharper edges without requiring a canonical coordinate system.

13885-visionnerf.md.name: VisionNeRF
13885-visionnerf.md.summary: VisionNeRF synthesizes novel views from a single unposed image by combining Vision Transformer and CNN features, using self-attention to resolve occlusion artifacts that degrade other methods.

13907-transnerf.md.name: TransNeRF
13907-transnerf.md.summary: TransNeRF is a generalizable neural radiance field method that synthesizes novel views using a Transformer framework to aggregate multi-view information, eliminating per-scene optimization.

12036-lisa.md.name: LISA

13842-humannerf.md.name: HumanNeRF

15640-humannerf-se.md.name: HumanNeRF-SE
15640-humannerf-se.md.summary: HumanNeRF-SE synthesizes novel human poses from monocular video using frozen SMPL weights and sparse encoding to reduce computational complexity and prevent overfitting.

14014-oponerf.md.name: OPONeRF

14073-mixer-nerf.md.name: Mixer-NeRF
14073-mixer-nerf.md.summary: Mixer-NeRF enhances NeRF by mixing spatial and channel features via an MLCA module and dynamically weighting them with an SE module to restore local detail.

14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimizat.name: Sparse View and Few-Shot Optimization

7371-simple-nerf.md.name: Simple-NeRF

11548-wah-nerf.md.name: WaH-NeRF

11859-deceptive-nerf-3dgs.md.name: Deceptive-NeRF/3DGS

12967-flipnerf.md.name: FlipNeRF

14429-mixture-of-experts-and-modular-arc.name: Mixture-of-Experts and Modular Architectures

14487-uncertainty-and-reliability.md.name: Uncertainty and Reliability
14487-uncertainty-and-reliability.md.summary: Uncertainty and Reliability methods extend NeRF to quantify prediction confidence by modeling aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty, enabling artifact filtering and reliable geometry assessment unlike standard deterministic rendering.

12968-uncertainty-aware-nerf.md.name: Uncertainty-aware NeRF
12968-uncertainty-aware-nerf.md.summary: Uncertainty-aware NeRF is a neural radiance field variant that predicts Gaussian distributions for color and depth, quantifying aleatoric uncertainty to reveal data reliability at the pixel level.

13768-ua-plantnerf-architecture.md.name: UA-PlantNeRF Architecture

12006-fig-nerf.md.name: Fig-NeRF
12006-fig-nerf.md.summary: Fig-NeRF is a scene composition model that uses separate deformable and latent-conditioned NeRFs to enable object interpolation and amodal segmentation.

13525-dm-nerf.md.name: DM-NeRF
13525-dm-nerf.md.summary: DM-NeRF reconstructs 3D scenes and decomposes objects from 2D images using an explicit object field for instance-level separation and an object manipulator for occlusion-aware editing.

14413-unified-decompositional-and-compos.name: Unified Decompositional and Compositional NeRF
14413-unified-decompositional-and-compos.summary: UDC-NeRF is a two-stage framework that jointly learns disentangled object-level and global scene representations to enable novel view synthesis and semantic editing.

14566-image-enhancement-and-restoration-.summary: These methods modify NeRF training to reconstruct sharp static scenes from defective inputs by explicitly modeling degradation or transients, unlike sibling methods that alter network topology or encoding.

11964-deblurnerf.md.name: DeblurNeRF
11964-deblurnerf.md.summary: DeblurNeRF reconstructs sharp NeRFs from blurry images by jointly optimizing the field and a learnable spatially-varying blur kernel, unlike methods using fixed priors.

13737-ie-nerf.md.name: IE-NeRF

14270-sharp-nerf.md.name: Sharp-NeRF
14270-sharp-nerf.md.summary: Sharp-NeRF is a grid-based NeRF framework that renders sharp images from blurry inputs using discrete learnable kernels and a sharpness prior, enabling significantly faster training than MLP-based methods.

14567-modular-hierarchical-and-latent-ar.name: Modular, Hierarchical, and Latent Architectures
14567-modular-hierarchical-and-latent-ar.summary: Modular, Hierarchical, and Latent Architectures extend NeRF by decoupling scene representation into specialized components or latent codes to model dynamic, stratified, or topologically complex environments.

13906-hypernerf.md.name: HyperNeRF
13906-hypernerf.md.summary: HyperNeRF models non-rigidly deforming scenes with topological variations by extending NeRF's 3D input space with higher-dimensional ambient coordinates.

14015-strata-nerf.md.name: Strata-NeRF
14015-strata-nerf.md.summary: Strata-NeRF is a neural radiance field method that uses discrete latent codes to model structural discontinuities in stratified scenes, avoiding the haziness artifacts common in standard continuous NeRFs.

14895-neuraleditor.md.name: NeuralEditor
14895-neuraleditor.md.summary: NeuralEditor edits neural radiance fields by intrinsically integrating point clouds, allowing users to manipulate scene geometry by moving points without retraining.

15007-murf-multi-baseline-radiance-field.name: MuRF (Multi-Baseline Radiance Fields)
15007-murf-multi-baseline-radiance-field.summary: MuRF is a feed-forward sparse view synthesis method that constructs a target-aligned frustum volume and uses a 3D context-aware decoder to handle large camera baselines.

15011-gaussian-and-primitive-based-repre.name: Gaussian and Primitive-Based Representations
15011-gaussian-and-primitive-based-repre.summary: Gaussian and Primitive-Based Representations replace implicit NeRF fields with explicit geometric primitives to enable real-time rasterization and geometric interpretability.

13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly..name: Differentiable Primitive Assembly
13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly..summary: Differentiable Primitive Assembly models 3D shapes as learnable quadric primitives using algebraic set operations, distinguishing itself from rasterization and point-based density fields.

15538-point-nerf-representation.md.name: Point-NeRF Representation
15538-point-nerf-representation.md.summary: Point-NeRF represents volumetric radiance fields using explicit neural point clouds, avoiding empty space sampling and using inverse-distance weighted aggregation of local features rather than set-theoretic operations or analytic splatting.

15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-re.name: Frequency-Modulated Point Cloud Rendering
15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-re.summary: Frequency-Modulated Point Cloud Rendering uses an Adaptive Frequency Net to predict per-point frequency and phase, enabling real-time, high-frequency detail reconstruction that is significantly faster than NeRF.

15032-decentralized-federated-nerf.md.name: Decentralized Federated NeRF
15032-decentralized-federated-nerf.md.summary: Decentralized Federated NeRF learns global 3D scenes from crowdsourced images by keeping personal data local and using secure aggregation to minimize server compute and prevent data leakage.

15220-neural-proxy.md.name: Neural Proxy
15220-neural-proxy.md.summary: Neural Proxy renders unseen animations without temporal learning by combining neural volume rendering with an animatable mesh proxy, unlike NeRF or Neural Texture.

15255-visnerf.md.name: ViSNeRF
15255-visnerf.md.summary: ViSNeRF is a hybrid neural radiance field method that efficiently synthesizes dynamic volumetric visualizations by combining explicit spatial feature grids with implicit MLP decoders using tensor factorization.

15441-ebad-nerf.md.name: EBAD-NeRF
15441-ebad-nerf.md.summary: EBAD-NeRF reconstructs sharp 3D radiance fields from motion-blurred images by jointly optimizing learnable camera poses and NeRF parameters using hybrid event-RGB data.

15497-dino-enhanced-nerf.md.name: DINO-enhanced NeRF
15497-dino-enhanced-nerf.md.summary: DINO-enhanced NeRF integrates pre-trained vision features into NeRF for few-shot 3D reconstruction, though it often underperforms the baseline due to feature-task mismatch.

15527-lora-fine-tuning-of-dino.md.name: LoRA Fine-Tuning of DINO
15527-lora-fine-tuning-of-dino.md.summary: LoRA Fine-Tuning of DINO adapts frozen DINOv2 features to NeRF geometry by training only low-rank matrices, enabling efficient few-shot 3D reconstruction.

15543-neurmips.md.name: NeurMiPs
15543-neurmips.md.summary: NeurMiPs represents 3D scenes as learnable planar experts, solving MPI limitations and NeRF blurring by combining explicit geometry with implicit appearance for superior extrapolation and real-time rendering.

15544-codenerf.md.name: CodeNeRF
15544-codenerf.md.summary: CodeNeRF is a neural radiance field that disentangles shape and texture via separate latent embeddings, enabling novel view synthesis and explicit editing of unseen objects from a single unposed image.

15546-dynamic-scene-and-temporal-modelin.name: Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling
15546-dynamic-scene-and-temporal-modelin.summary: Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling extends NeRF to represent time-varying scenes by augmenting inputs with temporal signals or deformation fields, avoiding static artifacts.

13848-gear-nerf.md.name: Gear-NeRF
13848-gear-nerf.md.summary: Gear-NeRF renders dynamic scenes by stratifying them into motion-based gears, using parallel 4D volumes to allocate higher sampling resolution to regions with larger motion scales.

14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md.name: NeRF with Time Parameter
14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md.summary: NeRF with Time Parameter adapts static NeRF for dynamic scenes by concatenating time encoding to spatial input, differing from complex methods via its minimal architectural modification.

15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-syn.name: Forward Warping for Novel View Synthesis
15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-syn.summary: Forward Warping renders dynamic scenes by warping a canonical field to target times, distinguishing itself from backward flow methods by simplifying deformation and handling mapping difficulties via average splatting and inpainting.

15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural.name: Dynamic Appearance Particle Neural Radiance Field
15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural.summary: DAP-NeRF synthesizes novel views of dynamic scenes from monocular video by applying appearance particles only to moving objects while keeping the background static, unlike ParticleNeRF which requires multi-view data.

15551-kfd-nerf.md.summary: KFD-NeRF is a dynamic NeRF method that uses a Kalman filter to separate motion estimation into observer and predictor branches, weighting them via a learnable gain.

16576-sls4d.md.name: SLS4D
16576-sls4d.md.summary: SLS4D is a 4D novel view synthesis method that reduces parameters by using a sparse latent space with attention-based spatial aggregation and dense time slots for temporal continuity.

18515-st-nerf.md.name: ST-NeRF

15989-conditional-and-latent-representat.summary: Conditional and Latent Representations extend NeRF with low-dimensional latent codes to enable generative modeling and disentangled control over shape and appearance, distinguishing it from standard single-scene reconstruction.

16793-disentangled-conditional-nerf.md.name: Disentangled Conditional NeRF
16793-disentangled-conditional-nerf.md.summary: Disentangled Conditional NeRF is a generative radiance field architecture that achieves independent control over 3D object shape and appearance by isolating their conditioning mechanisms.

18595-headnerf.md.name: HeadNerf

16591-scarf.md.summary: SCARF is a memory-efficient continual learning method for multiple 3D scenes that factorizes NeRF weights into shared and scene-specific components to prevent catastrophic forgetting.

18117-pl-nerf.md.summary: PL-NeRF is a NeRF variant for reconstructing power lines, distinguished by L-infinity spatial compression and integrated positional encoding to handle unbounded, thin structures.

16200-urbanir.md.name: UrbanIR

18127-unsupervised-decomposition-and-enh.summary: LLNeRF decomposes NeRF color into view-dependent lighting and view-independent color, enhancing lighting without ground truth by leveraging 3D geometry and multi-view consistency.

18647-samurai.md.name: SAMURAI
18647-samurai.md.summary: SAMURAI is a joint optimization framework that estimates 3D shape, BRDF, and illumination from unconstrained image collections by decomposing radiance and using a camera multiplex strategy to handle coarse pose annotations.

18360-generative-and-gan-based-methods.m.summary: Generative and GAN-Based Methods synthesize novel 3D objects by optimizing radiance fields to match pretrained 2D GAN distributions, enabling data augmentation and unseen object synthesis unlike standard NeRF reconstruction.

18126-lifting-2d-gan-to-3d-radiance-fiel.summary: Lifting 2D GAN to 3D Radiance Field distills 2D GAN knowledge into a shared NeRF using Generative Latent Optimization to generate photorealistic 3D objects with arbitrary poses.

18409-training-configuration-and-optimiz.summary: Training Configuration and Optimization defines the hyperparameters and schedules for NeRF training, focusing on learning dynamics rather than network topology.

14635-nerf-w-hyperparameter-configuratio.name: NeRF-W Hyperparameter Configuration
14635-nerf-w-hyperparameter-configuratio.summary: NeRF-W Hyperparameter Configuration specifies training settings for decomposing scenes into static geometry and transient appearance, distinguishing it from standard NeRF by explicitly modeling dynamic objects and varying lighting.

18140-neural-deformable-anchor-neuda.md.name: Neural Deformable Anchor (NeuDA)
18140-neural-deformable-anchor-neuda.md.summary: NeuDA is a neural implicit representation for high-fidelity surface reconstruction that replaces learnable feature vectors with optimized 3D positions, called anchors, to adaptively encode local geometry.

18147-neural-duplex-radiance-fields-ndrf.summary: Neural Duplex Radiance Fields distill pretrained NeRFs into a mesh-based representation using a shallow CNN and dual ray intersections to achieve real-time, high-quality view synthesis with significantly lower computational cost.

18457-mlp-network-architecture.md.summary: MLP Network Architecture maps encoded 3D coordinates to density and color using specific fully-connected layers and skip connections to process high-dimensional positional encodings.

13634-smt-parallelization-with-logical-r.summary: SMT Parallelization with Logical Ray Lists eliminates race conditions and cache trashing in SMT architectures by assigning distinct ray lists to each logical CPU per block, avoiding expensive synchronization.

8153-williams-distributed-projection.md.name: Williams Distributed Projection
8153-williams-distributed-projection.md.summary: Williams Distributed Projection is a parallel volume rendering technique that partitions datasets across multiple nodes to enable scalable rendering of massive volumes exceeding single-machine limits.

20155-group-wise-projection-release.md.name: Group-wise Projection Release
20155-group-wise-projection-release.md.summary: Group-wise Projection Release is a memory optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reduces peak memory by processing and immediately releasing 3x3 projection groups, distinguishing itself from Williams Distributed Projection through fine-grained release.

8387-cpu-gpu-memory-transfer-and-synchro.summary: CPU-GPU Memory Transfer and Synchronization moves Gaussian splatting data to discrete GPU memory via staging buffers, solving independent memory space issues by explicitly staging transfers unlike integrated GPU direct mapping.

9032-gpu-buffer-upload-via-transfer-buff.summary: GPU Buffer Upload via Transfer Buffer uses OpenGL PBO ping-pong buffering to asynchronously stream volume data, decoupling uploads from rendering to prevent CPU stalls without relying on dedicated copy engines.

9054-gpu-asynchronous-streaming.md.name: GPU Asynchronous Streaming
9054-gpu-asynchronous-streaming.md.summary: GPU Asynchronous Streaming uses separate OpenGL contexts and threads to overlap compute, download, and readback via the GPU's Copy Engine, avoiding stalls from blocking transfers.

10166-asynchronous-pipeline-overlap.md.name: Asynchronous Pipeline (Overlap)
10166-asynchronous-pipeline-overlap.md.summary: Asynchronous Pipeline overlaps SSD reads, data transfers, and GPU rendering using multi-threading to hide I/O latency, distinguishing itself from sequential methods by allowing rendering to proceed while data is still being fetched.

17179-overlapped-implementation.md.name: Overlapped Implementation
17179-overlapped-implementation.md.summary: The Overlapped Implementation is a rendering technique that hides data transfer overhead by fully overlapping data loading, volume slicing, and rendering. 20882-cuda-streams-and-pinned-memory-opt.summary: This optimization overlaps GPU computation with data transfers using CUDA streams and page-locked memory to eliminate synchronization stalls and maximize throughput.

9634-transform-feedback-gpgpu.md.name: Transform Feedback GPGPU

9704-multipass-partitioning-mpp.md.name: Multipass Partitioning (MPP)
9704-multipass-partitioning-mpp.md.summary: Multipass Partitioning splits shader dependency graphs into multiple passes to fit resource-constrained GPUs, minimizing runtime while respecting hardware limits.

9735-dynamic-programming-multipass-parti.summary: Dynamic Programming Multipass Partitioning (DPMPP) is a method for solving the resource-constrained GPU shader execution problem by partitioning a shader program's dependency graph (DAG) into multiple passes. 11538-megakernel-generation.md.name: Megakernel Generation
11538-megakernel-generation.md.summary: Megakernel generation consolidates differentiable rendering into a single GPU kernel, minimizing memory bandwidth by storing state in registers instead of using inter-kernel communication.

10234-warp-subgroup-level-primitives.md.name: Warp/Subgroup Level Primitives
10234-warp-subgroup-level-primitives.md.summary: Warp/Subgroup Level Primitives enable fast, lockless thread communication and aggregation within a GPU execution unit using registers, bypassing global memory latency and shared memory bottlenecks.

3683-subgroup-operations.md.name: Subgroup Operations
3683-subgroup-operations.md.summary: Subgroup operations are fast, hardware-synchronized collective computations within a warp or wave that exchange data via registers, avoiding the latency of global memory synchronization used by atomic operations.

4949-warp-shuffling.md.name: Warp Shuffling
4949-warp-shuffling.md.summary: Warp Shuffling is a warp-level reduction technique using hardware shuffle instructions to keep data in registers, eliminating shared memory allocation and synchronization barriers.

5523-double-buffer-shuffling.md.name: Double Buffer Shuffling
5523-double-buffer-shuffling.md.summary: Double Buffer Shuffling is a warp-level reduction technique that splits workload across two halves of a warp using dual buffers to mitigate active thread reduction issues found in single-buffer approaches.

8113-double-buffer-shared-warp-marching..name: Double Buffer Shared Warp Marching
8113-double-buffer-shared-warp-marching..summary: Double Buffer Shared Warp Marching is a GPU volume rendering technique that uses two buffers per thread to keep the entire warp active during reduction, improving execution efficiency over previous methods.

10224-warp-level-reduction.md.name: Warp-level Reduction
10224-warp-level-reduction.md.summary: Warp-level reduction aggregates update requests within a GPU warp to minimize redundant atomic operations, distinguishing itself by focusing on contention reduction for atomic primitives.

12357-adaptive-atomic-reduction-arc.md.name: Adaptive Atomic ReduCtion (ARC)
12357-adaptive-atomic-reduction-arc.md.summary: Adaptive Atomic ReduCtion (ARC) is a GPU primitive that accelerates differentiable rendering by performing warp-level reduction in registers to minimize L2 cache traffic, unlike prior methods that buffer atomics in L1 memory.

12371-adaptive-atomic-reduction-hardware.name: Adaptive Atomic ReduCtion Hardware (ARC-HW)
12371-adaptive-atomic-reduction-hardware.summary: ARC-HW is a hardware-software cooperative primitive that accelerates commutative atomic additions in differentiable rendering by performing warp-level reduction within the Streaming Multiprocessor and dynamically distributing remaining atomic computation between the SM and L2 ROP units.

12373-adaptive-atomic-reduction-software.name: Adaptive Atomic ReduCtion Software (ARC-SW)
12373-adaptive-atomic-reduction-software.summary: ARC-SW is a software-only framework that accelerates gradient computation in differentiable rendering by dynamically selecting between atomic addition and warp-level reduction to minimize GPU bottlenecks.

13060-gpu-offloaded-calculations.md.name: GPU Offloaded Calculations
13060-gpu-offloaded-calculations.md.summary: GPU Offloaded Calculations migrates bias and scale operations from CPU to GPU for faster volume rendering, distinct from general compute shaders by focusing on specific mathematical transformations in OpenGL pipelines.

13356-gpu-matrix-operations.md.name: GPU Matrix Operations
13356-gpu-matrix-operations.md.summary: GPU Matrix Operations offloads matrix inversion and transform-position calculations to the GPU to save CPU cycles, targeting static voxel scenes with mostly unchanged geometry.

14604-tiled-matrix-multiplication-with-s.summary: A GPU kernel that optimizes matrix multiplication C = A \times B by tiling data into block-private shared memory to reduce global memory bandwidth pressure. 16416-batched-fault-injection-engine.md.summary: The Batched Fault Injection Engine is a parallel workload that batches multiple corrupted variants of a scene into a single rasterizer call to saturate device throughput, removing latency bounds associated with host control between renders. 18286-hybrid-mpi-openmp-parallelization..name: Hybrid MPI + OpenMP Parallelization
18286-hybrid-mpi-openmp-parallelization..summary: Hybrid MPI + OpenMP parallelization combines distributed messaging with shared-memory threading to scale volume rendering on supercomputers while reducing inter-node communication overhead.

21565-parallel-partitioning-and-tiling.m.name: Parallel Partitioning and Tiling
21565-parallel-partitioning-and-tiling.m.summary: Parallel Partitioning and Tiling decomposes volume rendering workloads to balance computational load and memory bottlenecks, distinguishing itself by focusing on initial decomposition and load-balancing mechanisms rather than the final compositing stage.

2108-y-bucket-parallelization.md.name: Y-Bucket Parallelization
2108-y-bucket-parallelization.md.summary: Y-Bucket Parallelization is a scanline-based algorithm that groups polygons into y-buckets to maximize coherence and avoid ray-casting difficulties, unlike tile-based methods that break scanlines.

2123-parallel-direct-volume-rendering-wi.name: Parallel Direct Volume Rendering with Y-Buckets and X-Buckets
2123-parallel-direct-volume-rendering-wi.summary: Parallel Direct Volume Rendering with Y-Buckets and X-Buckets is a scanline-based algorithm that efficiently renders irregular grids by grouping polygons into y-buckets and x-buckets to maintain front-to-back visibility and maximize coherence.

2801-multi-core-bono-tree-traversal-and-.name: Multi-core BONO Tree Traversal and Ray Casting with Dynamic Tile Grouping
2801-multi-core-bono-tree-traversal-and-.summary: Multi-core BONO Tree Traversal and Ray Casting with Dynamic Tile Grouping is a parallel rendering technique that optimizes cache performance and load balancing by decoupling traversal from ray casting and dynamically grouping Z-ordered tiles based on estimated complexity.

5728-object-parallel-rendering.md.name: Object Parallel Rendering
5728-object-parallel-rendering.md.summary: Object Parallel Rendering partitions volume data across processors to enable large-scale rendering, distinguishing itself from image-space methods by distributing data rather than the screen.

13994-image-space-vs-object-space-parall.name: Image-Space vs Object-Space Parallelism
13994-image-space-vs-object-space-parall.summary: Image-Space vs Object-Space Parallelism distinguishes volume rendering task organization by whether tasks process pixels mapping back into data or data projecting forward to the screen.
